title: The Burning Bush
overview: Exodus Chapter 3 marks a pivotal moment in biblical history, where God reveals Himself to Moses through the miraculous burning bush. This chapter introduces God's personal name, "I AM THAT I AM," establishing His eternal and self-existent nature. God commissions Moses to deliver the Israelites from Egyptian bondage, promising divine presence and power despite Moses' initial doubts. The chapter sets the stage for the Exodus, highlighting God's awareness of His people's suffering and His plan for redemption. It emphasizes God's holiness, His covenant relationship with the patriarchs, and His sovereign authority to save and lead His people into the Promised Land.
structure:
**Verses 1-6: The Appearance at Horeb.** Moses encounters the burning bush on Mount Horeb, where God reveals Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, commanding Moses to remove his sandals because he stands on holy ground.

**Verses 7-12: God's Compassion and Commission.** God expresses His awareness of Israel's affliction and commissions Moses to lead them out of Egypt, assuring him of His presence and giving a sign of confirmation.

**Verses 13-22: The Divine Name and Instructions.** Moses questions God's name, receiving the revelation of "I AM THAT I AM." God instructs Moses to gather the elders and confront Pharaoh, foretelling resistance but promising deliverance and spoils from Egypt.

keyVerses.text: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals God's self-existence and eternal nature, providing Moses with the divine name to authenticate his mission. It underscores God's unchanging presence and authority, foundational for understanding His relationship with His people.

keyVerses.text: And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;
keyVerses.significance: God's declaration of awareness and compassion highlights His intimate involvement with His people's suffering. It affirms that God is not distant but actively engaged in history to bring deliverance.

keyVerses.text: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.
keyVerses.significance: God's promise of His presence reassures Moses amid doubt, emphasizing that divine accompaniment is essential for obedience and success. The reference to worship on the mountain connects to covenantal worship and God's holiness.

keyVerses.text: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
keyVerses.significance: This command highlights the holiness of God and the sacredness of the encounter. It teaches reverence and the recognition of God's sanctity in moments of divine revelation.

characters.name: Moses
characters.description: The central human figure, Moses is a shepherd called by God to lead Israel out of Egypt. His initial hesitation and questioning reveal his humility and the human struggle with divine calling.

characters.name: God (The LORD)
characters.description: God reveals Himself as the covenant God of the patriarchs, the compassionate deliverer aware of Israel's suffering. He commissions Moses and reveals His eternal name, asserting His sovereign authority.

characters.name: Angel of the LORD
characters.description: Appearing in the flame of fire within the burning bush, the Angel of the LORD represents God's presence and serves as the medium through which God communicates with Moses.

themes.description: God reveals Himself personally and powerfully through the burning bush and His name, emphasizing His holiness, eternal nature, and covenant faithfulness.
God’s awareness of Israel’s suffering and His promise to rescue them highlight His role as Redeemer and protector of His covenant people.
Moses’ doubts and God’s assurance of His presence teach that obedience to God’s call is empowered by His sustaining presence.
The command to remove sandals on holy ground underscores God’s purity and the reverence due to Him, setting a tone for sacred encounters.

historicalContext: This chapter is set during the Late Bronze Age, approximately the 15th century BC, in the region of Midian near Mount Horeb (Sinai Peninsula). Moses, living in exile as a shepherd, encounters God in a desert wilderness, a place often associated with divine revelation in the ancient Near East. The Israelites are enslaved in Egypt under Pharaoh’s oppressive regime, reflecting a socio-political context of foreign domination and harsh labor. The cultural practice of covenant naming and the significance of mountains as sacred meeting places with God are crucial for understanding the narrative’s theological depth.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God's sovereignty and covenant faithfulness in this chapter. God's self-identification as "I AM" underscores His eternal, unchanging nature, and His promise to be with Moses highlights the assurance of divine grace empowering obedience.

Dispensationalists focus on the literal fulfillment of God's promises to Israel, viewing this chapter as the initiation of God's redemptive plan for the nation through Moses, with a clear distinction between Israel and the Church.

Early Church Fathers often allegorized the burning bush as a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who bore Christ without being consumed. They also saw Moses’ call as a type of Christ’s mission to redeem His people.

crossReferences.connection: Jesus’ declaration 'Before Abraham was, I am' echoes God's self-identification in Exodus 3:14, affirming His divinity and eternal existence.
Stephen recounts Moses’ encounter with the burning bush, emphasizing God's call and promise to deliver Israel, reinforcing the chapter’s historical and theological significance.
Moses’ faith in obeying God’s call is highlighted, showing his trust in God’s presence and power as introduced in Exodus 3.
God’s intervention to save His people from oppression reflects the deliverance promised in Exodus 3.
Isaiah’s vision of God’s holiness parallels Moses’ encounter with holy ground, emphasizing reverence before God.

application: Trust in God’s presence when facing difficult tasks, knowing He empowers and guides His servants.
Approach God with reverence, recognizing His holiness in worship and daily life.
Respond to God’s call with obedience despite feelings of inadequacy or fear.
Remember God’s compassion for those who suffer and pray for deliverance in times of hardship.
Declare the name of God with confidence, knowing He is the eternal "I AM."
conclusion: Exodus Chapter 3 stands as a foundational moment of divine revelation and commissioning, revealing God's holy presence, compassionate nature, and sovereign power. Through the burning bush, God calls Moses to a daunting mission but assures him of His abiding presence and authority. The chapter invites believers to trust in God's eternal name, respond to His call with faith, and approach Him with reverence. Its enduring message encourages Christians to recognize God’s active involvement in history and their lives, inspiring obedience and confidence in His promises.
timeline: c. 1446 BC - The Exodus and Moses’ Call

definitions.definition: Another name for Mount Sinai, the mountain where God revealed Himself to Moses.
God’s self-existent, eternal name revealing His unchanging and sovereign nature.
A place set apart by God's presence, demanding reverence and purity from those who approach.
A theophany or manifestation of God’s presence often acting as His messenger.
A symbol of God’s purifying presence and power, visible but not consuming the bush.

outline.heading: The Burning Bush Encounter
outline.description: Moses tends Jethro’s flock and discovers the burning bush on Mount Horeb. God reveals Himself as the God of the patriarchs and commands Moses to recognize the holiness of the place.

outline.heading: God’s Compassion and Call to Deliverance
outline.description: God declares His awareness of Israel’s suffering and commissions Moses to lead their deliverance, promising His presence and a sign of confirmation.

outline.heading: The Divine Name and Mission Instructions
outline.description: Moses questions God’s name and receives the revelation of "I AM." God instructs Moses to gather Israel’s elders and confront Pharaoh, foretelling resistance but assuring ultimate victory and spoils.
